requirements.requirement: Three-node Galera cluster (node1, node2, node3) formed with writes through any member visible from the others
requirements.summary: All three nodes report wsrep_cluster_size=3 and wsrep_local_state_comment=Synced. Rows inserted via node1, node2, and node3 are each subsequently visible when queried from the other members, directly demonstrating multi-master write propagation.

requirements.requirement: Database remains available for writes when one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's mariadbd process was killed; node1 and node2 immediately showed cluster_size=2 with wsrep_cluster_status=Primary. A write issued on node1 during the outage succeeded and was confirmed present on node2, directly showing the cluster remained writable through a bounded single-member disruption.

requirements.requirement: Member automatically resynchronizes when it returns
requirements.summary: node3 was restarted via rc-service after being killed; log evidence shows an automatic mariabackup SST from donor node1, after which node3 reported cluster_size=3/Synced and its query of the test table returned the row that was written on node1 while node3 was down, confirming genuine automatic resynchronization of missed data.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the public task contract are satisfied with direct, final-state evidence: a working 3-node Galera cluster with verified cross-member write propagation, demonstrated write availability during a bounded single-node outage, and demonstrated automatic resynchronization (including recovery of data written during the outage) when the node returned. The independently required node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for all three nodes with matching pre/post boot-identity pairs that are corroborated by the fixed collector snapshots (after_executor boot IDs dd697d39/694cbcb9/6f8af2f7 match the executor's own captured values), each followed by confirmed cluster/quorum/data recovery, and a final full-cluster write/read check after all three restarts. The executor's process was messy — it took an extended troubleshooting detour diagnosing an actual rsync SST donor bug before switching to mariabackup — but this iterative recovery was directly in service of reaching the working end state and left the cluster in a healthy, verified condition. Minor unremoved debug configuration (wsrep_debug=1, custom log_error path) and an unused rsync package are the main hygiene residue.
limitations: The node3 'unavailability' during the availability test was induced by killing the mariadbd process (SIGTERM) rather than a harder failure mode (e.g., network partition or VM stop), so evidence covers process-level outage but not other failure classes.

A large volume of intermediate troubleshooting output was truncated in the captured command records, so some low-level details of the SST bug diagnosis could not be independently verified beyond the summarized log excerpts.

Package-health and failed-service checks in the fixed lifecycle snapshots show only 'chrony.drift' as a benign pre-existing diff and no failed-service data (systemctl unsupported on Alpine), limiting cross-validation of hygiene beyond what the executor timeline shows directly.

operational_hygiene.summary: The bulk of the executor's mutating activity (repeated /var/lib/mysql wipes, mariadb-install-db re-runs, kill -9 of stuck mariadbd/rsync processes, service zap/restart cycles) was directly tied to diagnosing and resolving a genuine rsync-SST donor-selection bug on this Alpine/Galera combination, and each cycle ended in a working, re-verified cluster state — this iterative recovery is treated as in-service of the material outcome rather than unnecessary experimentation. Two lower-severity residues remain from that troubleshooting, however: (1) wsrep_debug=1 and a custom log_error=/var/lib/mysql/mariadb.err were added to all three nodes' galera.cnf for debugging (cmd-8afbe28a57b44a45, cmd-e5545aceb1264eed, cmd-ee8854fe5b9c4ede) and were never removed, leaving verbose WSREP debug logging permanently enabled in production; (2) the rsync package was installed on all nodes for the original SST method that was later abandoned in favor of mariabackup, leaving an unused package installed (cmd-6ad3365ac5a14039 and node2/node3 equivalents). Both are low-risk, non-destructive, and don't weaken security or availability, but they are retained, task-unrelated residue. Temporary log files under /tmp (reboot.log, mysqld1.log, sst_log_archive/*) also remain but are inert and low-risk. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening actions were left in place; the sst_user account created for mariabackup SST auth has appropriately scoped privileges (RELOAD, LOCK TABLES, PROCESS, REPLICATION CLIENT) rather than superuser access.
